title: Normalized K-injective section complexes at closed lifted tests
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and on every small pro-etale site put $\Lambda_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use internal $\Lambda_Y$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], their exact inverse images and ordinary unbounded derived direct images computed on K-injectives [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. All sites and section values are taken in a common sufficiently large universe. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak a\subseteq A$ an ideal, $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $s:Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak a)\hookrightarrow U$. Let $v$ be the affine ind-etale closed-site lift [def-exc-closed-site-lift]. Let $V\to Z$ be an affine ind-etale object such that $V$ and $B=v(V)$ are w-contractible [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Let $f:X\to U$ be a morphism of affine schemes and put $X_Z=X\times_UZ$, with projections $h:X_Z\to X$, $f_Z:X_Z\to Z$. Put $T=X\times_UB$, $T_0=X\times_UV$ and $a:T_0\hookrightarrow T$; products mean scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$, let $\mathcal I$ be a K-injective representative of $K$, and let $j:h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$ be a quasi-isomorphism with $\mathcal J$ K-injective. Here K-injective means that every chain map from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic, and $Q$ denotes localization of complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Then $f_*\mathcal I$ and $(f_Z)_*\mathcal J$ are K-injective representatives of $Rf_*K$ and $R(f_Z)_*h^*K$, respectively. There are isomorphisms in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$
$$\begin{aligned}
R\Gamma(V,s^*Rf_*K)&\xrightarrow{\sim}Q((s^*f_*\mathcal I)(V))\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(\mathcal I(T)),\\
R\Gamma(V,R(f_Z)_*h^*K)&\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(((f_Z)_*\mathcal J)(V))=Q(\mathcal J(T_0)).
\end{aligned}$$
The second arrow in the first line is the inverse of the actual unit-section map $(f_*\mathcal I)(B)\to(s^*f_*\mathcal I)(V)$, followed by the section formula $(f_*\mathcal I)(B)=\mathcal I(T)$. The other arrows are the resolution comparisons for the universal right-derived units and exact evaluation at $V$.
The derived section-localization identifications give
$$Q(\mathcal I(T))\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(T,K|_T),\qquad Q(\mathcal J(T_0))\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(T_0,(h^*K)|_{T_0}).$$
They are normalized by the degreewise identities on localized sections. The canonical coefficient-compatible pullback composition identifies $(h^*K)|_{T_0}\cong a^*(K|_T)$. All displayed maps have these normalizations rather than arbitrary choices of isomorphisms.

proof.text: The exact inverse-image adjunctions preserve K-injective complexes under their right adjoints. Apply this to L and J. The canonical rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ on a K-injective is the inverse of rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso. Composing it with the image of the supplied representative isomorphism e, or pullRepresentative formed from j, proves invertibility of the two pushModel maps.

Use the proved internal_test_preservesHomology lemma underlying closed-test unit evaluation. It makes evaluation at the closed test exact and gives finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation. Thus the canonical universal derived unit is invertible on every complex, without requiring that closed pullback preserve K-injectivity. Exact inverse image applied to the pushModel comparison is invertible. Form leftMap and rightMap as the prescribed composites and take their asIso inverses; this gives the required inverse equations by reflexivity.

Use the existing internalSpecializationUnit_bijective calculation underlying closed-test unit evaluation: weak contractibility of the lift gives surjectivity of sheaf epimorphisms, and its closed-fibre square gives specialization of every lifted point to the fibre. Thus evaluation of the actual internal adjunction unit is invertible. The shared fiberIso makes closedFibreArrow an isomorphism, so evaluationMap along it is invertible. The original closedUnit is their composite, with the literal pushEvaluation identity. Every component of closedUnitComplex is therefore invertible; so is its image by Q. Taking its asIso inverse constructs eUnit with the required inverse equation by reflexivity.

For any small pro-etale object V of X, use the existing localization_sections_iso, module_weaklyEtale_preservesKInjective and derived_pullback_iso calculations in the weakly-etale derived-evaluation-restriction module. The equality of localizationSections with its closedFibreModuleSectionsRestriction is proved by extensionality and reflexivity, including the actual diagonal arrow and the actual module unit. Therefore derivedLocalization is invertible. On the supplied K-injective L the evaluation derived unit is invertible, and the final factor is the image of e. Their composite is localizationModel, proving both localization assertions for the actual test fibres. The site objects already carry their weakly-etale morphism proofs, so a separate ring-level ind-etale stability application is unnecessary.

The coefficient-compatible derived composition comparison is already the concrete definition derivedTestPullbackComposition in this module. It is the termwise descent of testPullbackComposition using the existing mapDerivedCategoryNatIso and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso, with their canonical localization factors. No further existential comparison or ringed-site localization theorem is required in the final conjunction.
